contract: Pure resolution of a recipe's declared module functions (name and version) against at most 256 caller-supplied manifests (name, version, description, arguments and result schemas, cost, permissions) with every reason given at once; a check of the arguments of a call and of its result through core/payload-schema, refusals located by function name and structural path; a SHA-256 identity of the resolved manifests; one workflow/tool-registry source. No call of a module, no Lua, no process, no discovery.
limits: No claim that a function exists or behaves as its manifest says: the manifests are the host's statement. A schema check says that a value has the declared form, not that a call is allowed or succeeded.

A refusal names the function and the structural path of core/payload-schema (a member is :key, an array position is its integer); the name of a member is never given, and at most 16 violations come in no fixed order.
The cost is an estimate that the manifest states; the Piece neither measures nor enforces it.
No bound on schema complexity or validation time beyond core/payload-schema; no check that a schema suits the module.
The identity is stable for the pinned Jason and OTP; it is not RFC 8785. Bindings are opaque plain data that only resolve/2 makes; a value from elsewhere is outside the Contract.
No Cure law is selected: the classification of a declared name is a restatement of lookups; lookup, bounds, canonical encoding and source form are finite tests.

grounding.claim: Seven named groups: resolve_at_load, arguments_located, results_checked_before_return, identity_changes_with_the_manifest, registry_source, names_fit_the_sandbox, bounds_and_redaction; temporary acceptance of a wrong version and a temporary skipped result check are negative controls (groups resolve_at_load and results_checked_before_return fail). Finite scenarios, not a universal proof.
Schema and argument or result checks reuse ready core/payload-schema with pinned JSV 0.27.0, draft 2020-12, no casting; the source reuses ready workflow/tool-registry unchanged.
Scalar and string encoding inside the private canonical JSON (keys sorted by bytes) of the identity.
SHA-256 of OTP crypto for the identity.
Pinned Elixir immutable maps, lists, binaries and anchored regular expressions.

The host supplies truthful manifests, one for each function that a module really offers, with schemas that it approved; an Adapter binding for each alias of the source; a caller that checks the arguments before it dispatches a call and the result before it records it for the replay; and, for workflow/recipe-check, the permissions and the estimate of each manifest with a unit equal to the unit of that check.

telemetry.contract: Pure functions emit no observations; the caller owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Intrinsic operands and fixed bounds only; no selectable settings.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; bindings are caller-owned plain data.
